questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The outcome of the Prophet's spiritual retreat to Cave Hira was the

options.text: commencement of the revelation of the Glorious Qur'an
award of a chieftaincy title by the Makkan aristocrats

questions.explanation: When Prophet Muhammad (SAW) retreated to Cave Hira near Makkah at age 40, Angel Jibril appeared to him with the first revelation of the Qur'an (Q. 96:1–5).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: One of the main lessons of the first revelation (Suratul-Alaq, Q. 96:1–5) is the

options.text: geographical description of the Arabian Peninsula
importance of seeking and disseminating knowledge through reading and the pen
military strategy for the Battle of Badr

questions.explanation: Qur'an 96:1–5 begins with the command 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' and highlights Allah teaching humanity by the pen.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The gradual spiritual and moral development of the early Muslim community was the wisdom behind the

options.text: compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr
standardization of the Qur'an under Uthman
piecemeal revelation of the Glorious Qur'an

questions.explanation: The Qur'an was revealed in stages over 23 years to strengthen the Prophet's heart and gradually instill Islamic faith, morals, and law.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: 'Verily, We have sent down the Reminder (al-Qur'an), and surely We will guard it' (Q. 15:9). The verse above refers to the

options.text: divine preservation of the Glorious Qur'an
translation of the Qur'an into foreign languages

questions.explanation: Qur'an 15:9 is the divine guarantee that Allah Himself protects the Glorious Qur'an from corruption or loss.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The battle in 633 CE in which many Huffaz (memorizers of the Qur'an) were martyred, prompting the first official compilation of the Qur'an, was fought at
questions.explanation: Many Huffaz died in the Battle of Yamamah against Musaylimah during Caliph Abu Bakr's reign, leading Umar ibn al-Khattab to advise compiling the Qur'an into a single volume.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The committee appointed by Caliph Uthman ibn Affan to standardize the Mushaf of the Glorious Qur'an consisted of
questions.explanation: Caliph Uthman appointed a four-member committee headed by Zayd ibn Thabit, alongside Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-As, and Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Harith.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: A common characteristic of Makkan chapters (Suwar) of the Glorious Qur'an is that they

options.text: are generally very long and deal with civil law
primarily address the hypocrites of Madinah
contain short, rhythmic verses and frequent oaths emphasizing Tawhid and the Hereafter
give detailed regulations on warfare and treaties

questions.explanation: Makkan suwar typically feature concise verses, powerful oaths, and emphasis on Tawhid, prophethood, and accountability on the Day of Judgment.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The fulfillment of the prophecy of the Roman victory over the Persians within a few years as foretold in Suratul-Rum (Q. 30:2–4) is an evidence of the

options.text: purely historical nature of the Qur'an
divine authenticity of the Glorious Qur'an

questions.explanation: The accurate fulfillment of the prophecy in Q. 30:2–4 demonstrates the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'an.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The Glorious Qur'an is comprehensive and distinct among revealed scriptures because

options.text: it is used solely as a book of supplications
complete spiritual, moral, social, economic and legal guidance are found in it
it was revealed in a single night in bound book form

questions.explanation: The Qur'an is a complete code of life encompassing creed, worship, ethics, family law, socio-economic justice, and governance.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) did not leave the Glorious Qur'an bound in a single book volume during his lifetime primarily because

options.text: he wanted only the Quraysh to inherit the text
revelation continued piecemeal at intervals up to shortly before his death
none of his companions knew how to write
writing materials were prohibited in Madinah

questions.explanation: Because revelation was still ongoing until shortly before the Prophet's demise, the complete text was compiled into a single bound volume (Suhuf) after his passing.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The correct meaning of Tafsir is the

options.text: detailed explanation, exegesis and commentary of the Glorious Qur'an
memorization of the Qur'an without understanding
recitation of the Qur'an in seven dialects

questions.explanation: Tafsir is the science of explaining and interpreting the meanings, context (Asbab an-Nuzul), and rulings of the Glorious Qur'an.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Tajwid, as one of the sciences of the Glorious Qur'an, is important because

options.text: it replaces the need for Tafsir
it deals only with the biography of the compilers
it provides the rules for correct articulation, pronunciation and recitation of the Glorious Qur'an
it translates the Qur'an into vernacular languages

questions.explanation: Tajwid preserves the proper phonetic articulation (Makharij) and rules of reciting the Qur'an as revealed to the Prophet (SAW).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: In the rules of Tajwid, pronouncing the letter Ra (ر) with a heavy, full-mouth resonance when it carries a Fathah or Dammah is known as
questions.explanation: Tafkhim means velarization or heavy pronunciation (such as Ra with Fathah or Dammah), whereas Tarqiq means light pronunciation.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The only Surah in the Glorious Qur'an that must be recited in every unit (Rak'ah) of obligatory prayer (Salah) is
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) stated: 'There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book (Suratul-Fatihah).'

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: 'Therefore turn in prayer to your Lord and sacrifice to Him alone' (Q. 108:2). The verse above is from
questions.explanation: Fa salli li-Rabbika wanhar ('So pray to your Lord and sacrifice [to Him alone]') is the second verse of Suratul-Kawthar (Q. 108:2).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Suratul-Ma'un (Q. 107) condemns those who neglect their prayers, make a show of charity, and

options.text: travel for trade in winter and summer
repulse the orphan and fail to encourage feeding the needy

questions.explanation: Suratul-Ma'un reproaches those who deny the Day of Account, mistreat orphans, neglect encouraging the feeding of the poor, and are heedless/ostentatious in prayer.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The vivid description of charging war-steeds panting and striking sparks of fire, illustrating human ingratitude to Allah, is the theme of
questions.explanation: Suratul-Adiyat (Q. 100) opens with an oath by the charging steeds and highlights human ingratitude and love of wealth.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The allegorical (Mutashabihat) and complex verses of the Glorious Qur'an are properly explained through the

options.text: Tafsir of the Glorious Qur'an by qualified scholars

questions.explanation: Sound Tafsir grounded in the Qur'an, authentic Sunnah, and scholarly knowledge is required to understand complex Qur'anic passages.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Hadith 3 of Imam an-Nawawi's Forty Hadith teaches that Islam is built upon
questions.explanation: Hadith 3 of An-Nawawi narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar states that Islam is built upon five pillars: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Hajj, and fasting Ramadan.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: A central teaching of the 10th Hadith of Imam an-Nawawi ('Allah the Almighty is Good and accepts only that which is good') is that

options.text: wealth alone guarantees acceptance of supplications
prayers are accepted only in Makkah
consuming lawful (Halal) sustenance and abstaining from the unlawful is a prerequisite for answered prayers

questions.explanation: Hadith 10 mentions a dusty traveler raising his hands in supplication while his food, drink, and clothing are Haram, asking how his prayer can be answered.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: 'Do not become angry.' In the 16th Hadith of Imam an-Nawawi, when a man asked the Prophet (SAW) for advice, the Prophet repeated this counsel
questions.explanation: In Hadith 16 narrated by Abu Hurayrah, a man asked the Prophet (SAW), 'Advise me,' and the Prophet repeated 'Do not become angry' several times.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: What differentiates Hadith Qudsi from Hadith Nabawi is that in Hadith Qudsi

options.text: it is recited as a Surah in obligatory Salah
there is no chain of narrators (Isnad)
the meaning is directly attributed to Allah while the wording is narrated by the Prophet (SAW)
it deals exclusively with commercial law

questions.explanation: In a Hadith Qudsi (Sacred Hadith), the Prophet (SAW) attributes the statement to Allah ('Allah Almighty said...'), whereas its phrasing is the Prophet's narration.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: One of the structural features of Sahih al-Bukhari is that the Ahadith are arranged into

options.text: thematic books (Kutub) and chapters (Abwab) according to Fiqh topics

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari is a Musannaf/Jami' work organized into thematic books and chapters with juristic chapter headings.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Which of the following collections from the Sihah Sittah focuses specifically on Ahkam (legal traditions of permissions, obligations and prohibitions)?
questions.explanation: Sunan Abi Dawud (one of the Six Authentic Books) was compiled specifically around legal traditions (Ahadith al-Ahkam).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: In Qur'an 17:23–24, immediately after commanding exclusive worship of Allah, believers are enjoined to show

options.text: kindness, humility and dutifulness to parents (Birrul-Walidayn)

questions.explanation: Qur'an 17:23 pairs the command to worship none but Allah with showing utmost kindness and respect to one's parents, especially in their old age.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The Children of Israel were admonished not to mix truth with falsehood or conceal the truth knowingly in
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:42 states: 'And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know [it].'

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Islam encourages every Muslim to earn a lawful livelihood through
questions.explanation: Islam upholds the dignity of labour; the Prophet (SAW) taught that nobody eats better food than that earned by the work of one's own hands.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Islam as a strictly monotheistic religion requires every believer to

options.text: venerate saints as intermediaries to God
worship and serve Allah alone without associating partners with Him
fast every day of the year

questions.explanation: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah requires directing all acts of worship exclusively to Allah without any partner (Shirk).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Consulting fortune-tellers and diviners (Kahins) is forbidden in Islam because

options.text: it ascribes knowledge of the unseen (Al-Ghayb) and divine power to creatures
it is practiced only at night

questions.explanation: Knowledge of the unseen (Al-Ghayb) belongs exclusively to Allah, so believing fortune-tellers violates Tawhid.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Which of the following practices constitutes Shirk (associating partners with Allah) in Islam?

options.text: Participating in idolatrous masquerade cults and veneration of ancestral spirits

questions.explanation: Venerating idols, ancestral spirits, or masquerade cults alongside Allah is an act of Shirk.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The Suhuf (Scrolls) mentioned in Suratul-A'la (Q. 87:18–19) were revealed to
questions.explanation: Qur'an 87:19 explicitly mentions the Suhuf (Scrolls) of Ibrahim and Musa (AS).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: In Islam, the fundamental Articles of Faith (Arkan al-Iman) are
questions.explanation: The six articles of faith are belief in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and Divine Decree (Qadar).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Delivering the two-part sermon (Khutbah) before the prayer is an essential condition for the validity of
questions.explanation: In Salatul-Jumu'ah, the Imam delivers the two-part Khutbah prior to leading the two-rak'ah congregational prayer.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: One of the fundamental conditions that make obligatory prayer (Salah) binding upon a Muslim is
questions.explanation: Salah is obligatory upon every Muslim who is sane (Aqil) and has reached the age of puberty/maturity (Baligh).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The recommended voluntary fast of Ashura is observed on the
questions.explanation: Ashura is observed on the 10th of Muharram (ideally paired with the 9th or 11th) in gratitude to Allah.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: According to the Hadith of the Prophet (SAW), Ayyam at-Tashriq (the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah) are days of
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) described the days of Tashriq as days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of Allah (Dhikr), and prohibited fasting on them.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The minimum number of upright adult male witnesses required for a valid marriage contract (Nikah) in Sunni jurisprudence is
questions.explanation: A valid Islamic marriage contract requires the presence of at least two upright adult male witnesses.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Literally, the Arabic term Shari'ah means

options.text: a clear, well-trodden path leading to a watering place

questions.explanation: Linguistically, Shari'ah denotes a clear, straight path to water, and technically refers to the divine law ordained by Allah.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Which of the founders of the four Sunni schools of jurisprudence was imprisoned for refusing a state judgeship and died in prison in 150 AH?
questions.explanation: Imam Abu Hanifah (Nu'man ibn Thabit) was imprisoned for his principled refusal to serve as Qadi under the Abbasid caliph Al-Mansur and died in 150 AH.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The overarching objective of the Islamic economic system is to

options.text: monopolize wealth in the hands of the state
promote social justice, lawful earning and equitable circulation of wealth

questions.explanation: Islamic economics prohibits exploitation (Riba, Gharar, hoarding) and promotes Zakah and fair trade so wealth does not circulate solely among the rich (Q. 59:7).

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: One of the socio-economic consequences of Riba (usury/interest) is that it

options.text: discourages productive effort and exploits the needy

questions.explanation: Riba allows lenders to accumulate guaranteed returns without sharing risk or productive labour, exploiting borrowers.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Mas'uliyyah (accountability) as a principle of the Islamic political system serves primarily to check

options.text: abuse of power and misappropriation of public trust

questions.explanation: Mas'uliyyah holds leaders accountable before Allah and the community (Ummah) to prevent corruption and misuse of public resources.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: In Qur'an 9:4, Allah commands Muslims to honour and fulfill treaties made with non-Muslims as long as the latter do not

options.text: violate the terms of the treaty or aid enemies against them

questions.explanation: Islam strictly enjoins fulfilling covenants and treaties with non-Muslims so long as they honour the agreement and do not support aggression.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: During the Jahiliyyah era, the most famous annual trade and poetic fair near Makkah was held at
questions.explanation: Souq Ukaz was the celebrated annual market and poetry festival in pre-Islamic Arabia.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: In pre-Islamic Arabia (Jahiliyyah), some Arab tribes practiced female infanticide (Wa'd al-Banat) mainly out of

options.text: fear of poverty and perceived social disgrace in war

questions.explanation: During the Jahiliyyah period, female infants were buried alive out of fear of poverty (Q. 17:31) and false pride regarding capture in tribal wars.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: On his childhood trade journey to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib, the person who recognized the signs of prophethood in young Muhammad (SAW) at Busra was the
questions.explanation: The Christian monk Bahira recognized the seal and signs of prophethood in the young Muhammad (SAW) during the caravan stop at Busra.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: Members of the Prophet's household and close circle (such as Khadijah, Ali, Zayd and Abu Bakr) embraced Islam immediately on the basis of his

options.text: known truthfulness, trustworthiness (Al-Amin) and upright character

questions.explanation: Those who knew the Prophet (SAW) best accepted his message without hesitation because of his impeccable integrity and truthfulness.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The reformist teachings and Jihad of Shaykh Uthman dan Fodio in Hausaland were primarily directed against

options.text: syncretism (mixing Islam with pagan practices) and un-Islamic oppression

questions.explanation: Shaykh Uthman dan Fodio campaigned against syncretism, illegal taxation, and corruption among the Hausa rulers, calling for a return to pure Sunnah.

questions.subject: irk
questions.question: The renowned ruler of the Mali Empire who promoted Islamic scholarship, built mosques in Timbuktu and Gao, and instituted regular Friday congregational prayers was
questions.explanation: Mansa Kankan Musa (r. 1312–1337) famously performed the Hajj in 1324, built mosques, established Friday prayers, and attracted Muslim scholars to Mali.
